endorsements.quote: Should stakeholders determine that an XAI architecture still is the optimal choice for decision support in the clinical setting, they are advised to conduct a more thorough examination of the clinical context to ascertain the extent to which the explanations provided by the system can enhance clinical judgement within the specific field of deployment.

unlisted_practices: Limit regulatory demands for explainable AI to instances where deployment in specific clinical circumstances does not give rise to reasonable doubt or contravene scientific research evidence.
Include exclusionary provisions in policy guidelines calling for XAI, so that specific circumstances such as time-sensitive settings can be exempted.
Collect further evidence on how explainability methods affect physicians' accuracy, confidence and trust in time-sensitive environments compared with non-XAI systems.
Prefer high-performing, well-designed black-box AI over XAI in inherently time-critical settings where clinicians cannot meaningfully evaluate explanations.
Have policy-makers who advocate for XAI determine whether excluding explainability methods is warranted in the case at hand.

screen.reason: Ethical and conceptual analysis questioning blanket endorsement of explainable AI (XAI) in time-sensitive clinical environments such as surgery.
